memo.text: Revenue was $25.17 billion, $4.02 billion below forecast. Automotive sales were $2.59 billion below forecast; the revenue bridge attributes $1.28 billion to lower volume and $1.31 billion to price/mix. Regulatory credits were $450.3 million below forecast, and energy generation and storage was $623.1 million below forecast, partly offset by leasing $63.2 million above forecast. Gross profit was $4.44 billion, $1.28 billion below forecast, while gross margin was 2.0 percentage points below forecast. The gross-profit bridge shows the largest shortfall in automotive at $1.14 billion, with energy and services also below forecast by $26.0 million and $113.4 million, respectively. Operating income was $2.06 billion, $710.7 million below forecast. Operating expenses were $572.6 million below forecast, including lower research and development expense by $365.2 million and selling, general and administrative expense by $203.8 million, cushioning the gross-profit miss. Free cash flow was $2.06 billion, $1.14 billion above forecast: operating cash flow was $1.33 billion above forecast, more than offsetting capital spending $193.5 million above forecast.

Revenue was $21.30 billion, $5.82 billion (21.5%) below the $27.12 billion base forecast. The revenue bridge attributes $5.16 billion of the shortfall to volume and $340.8 million to price/mix; deliveries were 386,810, 118.7 thousand below forecast, while automotive ASP was $42,553 per vehicle, $881 per vehicle below forecast (2.0%). Gross profit of $3.70 billion was $1.21 billion below forecast; automotive gross profit was the main drag at $1.23 billion below forecast, partly offset by energy's $89.6 million favorable bridge, while services and other reduced gross profit by $76.2 million. Gross margin was 17.4%, down 0.8 percentage points from forecast. Operating income of $1.17 billion was $965.7 million below forecast; operating expenses were $249.2 million below forecast, cushioning the gross-profit miss. Free cash flow was negative $2.53 billion, $3.62 billion below forecast: operating cash flow was $242 million, $3.07 billion below forecast, and capital expenditures were $2.77 billion, $548.5 million above forecast.

Revenue was $25.50 billion, $2.04 billion above forecast. Energy generation and storage was the largest positive revenue bridge at $1.37 billion above forecast, with volume adding $754 million and regulatory credits adding $527 million; price/mix reduced revenue by $521 million and services and other by $123 million. Deliveries were 443,956 vehicles, 17.6 thousand above forecast, while automotive ASP was $41,700 per vehicle, 2.7% below forecast. The revenue result therefore reflected stronger volume and energy, alongside lower automotive pricing and mix.

Gross profit was $4.58 billion, $484 million above forecast, and gross margin was 0.5 percentage points above forecast. Energy contributed $373 million of the gross-profit beat, versus $79.9 million from automotive and $30.9 million from services and other. Operating income was $1.61 billion, $740 million above forecast. Operating expenses came in $256 million below forecast, including research and development $549 million below and selling, general and administrative $350 million below forecast. Free cash flow was $1.34 billion, $996 million above forecast. Operating cash flow exceeded forecast by $866 million, while property and equipment purchases were $130 million below forecast. Cash generation was thus the key support for the free-cash-flow variance, with lower capital spending also contributing.

Revenue was $25.18 billion, $1.22 billion below forecast. Deliveries were 462,890 vehicles, 48.5 thousand above forecast; volume added $2.06 billion to revenue in the bridge. That benefit was tempered by automotive ASP of $40,700 per vehicle, $1,714 per vehicle below forecast, and regulatory credits $1.09 billion below forecast. Energy generation and storage revenue was also $1.44 billion below forecast. Gross profit reached $5.00 billion, $271 million above forecast; automotive gross profit contributed $341 million above forecast, partly offset by a $186 million energy gross-profit shortfall. Gross margin was 19.8%, up 1.9 percentage points versus forecast. Operating income was $2.72 billion, $1.57 billion above forecast. Operating expenses were $1.30 billion below forecast, including research and development $237 million below and selling, general and administrative expense $204 million below forecast. Free cash flow was $2.74 billion, $2.31 billion above forecast. Operating cash flow exceeded forecast by $3.37 billion, while property and equipment purchases were $1.06 billion above forecast, partly offsetting that benefit.

Revenue was $25.71 billion, $3.55 billion below the $29.25 billion base forecast, a 12.1% shortfall. The main revenue pressure was automotive: sales were $18.66 billion, $2.93 billion below forecast, with price/mix $2.10 billion below and volume $834.9 million below forecast. Energy generation and storage revenue was $3.06 billion, $163.5 million below forecast; automotive regulatory credits were $692 million, $143.0 million below forecast. Gross profit came to $4.18 billion, $1.15 billion below forecast, as the automotive gross-profit bridge was $1.05 billion adverse; gross margin was 16.3%, down 2.0 percentage points from forecast. Operating income was $1.58 billion, $1.35 billion below forecast; operating expenses were $2.60 billion, $198.9 million above forecast, including research and development at $1.28 billion, $301.0 million above forecast. Free cash flow was $2.03 billion, $1.13 billion above forecast, supported by operating cash flow of $4.81 billion, $1.19 billion above forecast; capital spending was $2.78 billion, $67.5 million above forecast.

Revenue was $19.34 billion, $7.09 billion (26.8%) below the base forecast. Automotive sales were $12.93 billion, $3.16 billion (19.6%) below forecast; deliveries were 336,681 vehicles, 14.9% below forecast, and automotive ASP was $38,389 per vehicle, 5.6% below forecast. The revenue bridge shows volume $2.40 billion below forecast and price and mix $763 million below, alongside regulatory credits $509 million below forecast. Energy generation and storage revenue was $2.73 billion, $2.64 billion (49.1%) below forecast; services and other was $2.64 billion, $824.7 million below. Gross profit of $3.15 billion was $1.69 billion (35.0%) below forecast, with automotive, energy and services gross-profit bridge impacts of $974 million, $623 million and $97.6 million below, respectively. Gross margin was 16.3%, 2.0 percentage points below forecast. Operating income was $399 million, $1.61 billion (80.2%) below forecast; operating expenses were $82.0 million below forecast, partly offsetting gross-profit pressure, while research and development was $85.2 million above forecast. Free cash flow was $664 million, $232 million (25.9%) below forecast, as operating cash flow was $1.57 billion below forecast, partly offset by capital purchases $1.34 billion below forecast.

Revenue was $22.50 billion, $2.02 billion below base forecast, an 8.2% shortfall. The largest revenue drags were energy generation and storage, $1.88 billion below forecast, and regulatory credits, $542 million below; automotive sales were $479 million above forecast, with ASP $1,484 per vehicle above forecast. Gross profit was $3.88 billion, $560 million below forecast, with energy contributing a $426 million shortfall, automotive a $118 million shortfall, and services and other a $16.2 million shortfall. Gross margin was 17.2%, 0.9 percentage points below forecast, reflecting the weaker gross-profit result against revenue. Operating income was $923 million, $624 million below forecast. The gross-profit gap and higher R&D and SG&A weighed on operating income, partly offset by a $279 million favorable impact from restructuring and other. Operating cash flow was $2.54 billion, $1.67 billion below forecast; capital spending was $2.39 billion, $120 million below forecast, but free cash flow still came to only $146 million, $1.55 billion below forecast. The cash flow variance was therefore driven chiefly by the operating cash flow shortfall, with lower capital spending providing only a partial offset.

Revenue was $28.10 billion, $5.73 billion above the $22.37 billion base forecast. The revenue beat was led by $3.81 billion from volume and $746 million from price and mix, with energy generation and storage adding $880 million above forecast. Gross profit was $5.05 billion, $1.24 billion above forecast; gross margin reached 18.0%, a 1.0 percentage-point improvement against forecast. The gross-profit contributions were $716 million from automotive, $345 million from energy, and $182 million from services and other. Operating income was $1.62 billion, $444 million above forecast, even as operating expenses ran $800 million above forecast. Research and development was $335 million below forecast and selling, general and administrative expense was $194 million above; a $941 million restructuring-and-other drag further offset the gross-profit gain. Free cash flow reached $3.99 billion, $2.59 billion above forecast: operating cash flow contributed a $2.30 billion favorable variance, while lower property-and-equipment purchases added $296 million. Overall, stronger revenue and cash generation more than absorbed the operating-cost and restructuring headwinds.

Revenue was $24.90 billion, $4.91 billion below the $29.81 billion base forecast, with the shortfall concentrated in automotive volume. Deliveries were 418,227 vehicles, 114.0 thousand below forecast, and automotive sales missed by $4.28 billion; favorable price/mix of $220 million and $240 million more regulatory-credit revenue partly cushioned the $4.50 billion volume shortfall. Energy generation and storage revenue was $473 million below forecast, while services and other was $368 million below.

Gross profit was $5.01 billion, $112 million below forecast, despite a 20.1% gross margin versus 17.2% forecast, a 2.9-percentage-point improvement. Automotive gross profit was $36.5 million below forecast and energy gross profit was $149 million below, partly offset by services gross profit $73.8 million above.

Operating expenses were $3.60 billion, $813 million below forecast; lower research and development and selling, general and administrative spending supported operating income of $1.41 billion, $702 million above forecast. Free cash flow was $1.42 billion, $289 million below forecast: operating cash flow was $124 million below plan and property-and-equipment purchases were $165 million above. Overall, stronger margin and lower operating expenses softened the impact of weak revenue on operating income, but did not prevent free cash flow from missing plan.

Revenue was $22.39 billion, $2.50 billion above forecast (12.6%). Automotive sales were $15.47 billion, $4.07 billion above forecast, reflecting volume $2.96 billion above forecast and price/mix $1.11 billion above forecast; deliveries were 358,023 vehicles, 73.9 thousand above forecast, while automotive ASP was $43,200 per vehicle, $3,094 per vehicle above forecast. These gains were partly offset by energy generation and storage revenue of $2.41 billion, $1.59 billion below forecast (39.8%). Gross profit reached $4.72 billion, $1.10 billion above forecast, and gross margin of 21.1% exceeded forecast by 2.9 percentage points. Automotive gross profit added $1.26 billion versus forecast, while energy gross profit was $240 million below forecast; services and other added $80.4 million. Operating expenses were $3.78 billion, $637 million below forecast, including R&D $294 million below forecast, supporting operating income of $941 million, $1.74 billion above forecast. Operating cash flow was $3.94 billion, $250 million above forecast, but property and equipment purchases were $2.49 billion, $361 million above forecast; free cash flow was $1.44 billion, $111 million below forecast (7.1%).

Revenue reached $28.24 billion, $3.13 billion above the base forecast. Volume added $2.96 billion, while energy generation and storage revenue was $393.8 million above forecast and services and other revenue was $258.9 million below forecast. Automotive sales were $3.12 billion above forecast, with deliveries of 480,126 vehicles versus a forecast 408.5 thousand; automotive ASP was $338 per vehicle above forecast. Regulatory credits were $137.9 million below forecast. Gross profit was $4.75 billion, $130.1 million above forecast: automotive and services gross-profit contributions were ahead of forecast, more than offsetting energy's $251.5 million shortfall. Gross margin was 16.8%, 1.6 percentage points below forecast, limiting the conversion of revenue strength into gross-profit growth. Operating income was $398 million, $498.8 million above forecast, helped by operating expenses $368.7 million below forecast, including SG&A $368.2 million below. Free cash flow was negative $1.09 billion, $2.84 billion below forecast. Operating cash flow exceeded forecast by $565 million, but purchases of property and equipment were $3.41 billion above forecast.

answers.text: Revenue missed forecast mainly because automotive volume was materially lower than assumed. The volume bridge contribution was $5.59 billion below forecast, while automotive sales overall were $5.67 billion below. Deliveries were 134.8 thousand below forecast, a 21.7% shortfall. Beyond vehicles, services and other revenue was $1.10 billion below forecast and energy generation and storage was $720 million below. Leasing contributed a modest positive variance, but that was not enough to offset the larger volume and other segment gaps.

Gross margin was 19.6%, 0.9 percentage points above forecast. That relative resilience sits alongside a gross-profit shortfall of $1.14 billion. The bridge identifies automotive as the largest negative contributor, at $1.14 billion below its forecast contribution, with energy also negative by $126 million. Services and other provided a $124 million positive offset. Thus, the margin comparison was favorable even though the dollar gross-profit result was below plan, reflecting the mix of segment-level outcomes rather than broad-based outperformance.

Regulatory credits generated $113 million of revenue, but the amount was $10.5 million, or 8.5%, below forecast. Credits therefore provided a revenue contribution, but not the full amount built into the forecast. Their shortfall was small beside the much larger automotive volume gap, so credits did not materially change the overall revenue variance. They remain relevant to interpreting the reported top line because they are a distinct revenue source and can cushion, or fail to cushion, weakness elsewhere in automotive sales.

Energy generation and storage revenue was $2.88 billion, $720 million below forecast, a 20.0% shortfall. Its gross-profit contribution was also below forecast, by $126 million. In other words, the segment added revenue, but it did not deliver the expected revenue scale or gross-profit dollars in the quarter. That made energy a meaningful secondary drag on the consolidated gross-profit bridge, although the automotive gross-profit shortfall was substantially larger.

Operating expenses were $4.78 billion, $807.8 million below forecast. Research and development was $122.5 million below plan, while selling, general and administrative expense was $535.8 million below plan. These undershoots cushioned the gross-profit weakness: the operating-income bridge shows positive offsets from both categories, as well as restructuring and other. Even with that expense discipline, operating income remained $332.6 million below forecast because the negative gross-profit contribution was larger than the combined favorable expense variances.

Free cash flow was $1.53 billion, $90.5 million above forecast, or 6.3%. Operating cash flow exceeded forecast by $1.59 billion. That benefit was partly offset by property and equipment purchases running $1.50 billion above forecast, a 46.5% overshoot. The net result was a modest free-cash-flow beat despite the heavier capital outlay. The cash-flow performance was therefore stronger than the operating-income comparison, with the operating cash contribution more than covering the adverse investment-spending variance.

Across the 12 published quarters, operating income was the hardest of the three listed measures to forecast by average absolute percentage error. Its 12-quarter average error was 101.0%, compared with 20.6% for gross profit and 17.1% for total revenue. The gap is pronounced: average operating-income error was substantially higher than the other two measures. This indicates that, in this backtest set, operating income estimates were less reliable on a percentage-error basis than revenue or gross-profit estimates; it does not identify the cause of that forecasting difficulty.

The backtest reports average absolute percentage errors across the 12 published quarters of 17.1% for total revenue, 20.6% for gross profit, and 101.0% for operating income. On that measure, revenue has the lowest average error, gross profit is somewhat higher, and operating income is markedly less accurate. Overall model accuracy is therefore uneven across the income statement, rather than captured well by a single score. These averages describe historical forecast errors in the supplied backtest and do not establish how the model will perform in a future quarter.

The bear case assumes 559.2 thousand deliveries and automotive sales of $22.03 billion, with automotive ASP at $39,399 per vehicle. It also uses a 17.7% gross margin and projects operating income of about $33.7 million. In that scenario, operating income is positive but close to break-even in scale compared with the other reported operating figures. The scenario captures a lower-volume, lower-margin outcome; these are forecast assumptions, not reported results for the quarter.

Next quarter, I would monitor deliveries and automotive sales alongside automotive ASP, to distinguish volume changes from price and mix. I would also track energy generation and storage revenue and services and other revenue, since both fell short of the current-quarter forecast. Gross margin and segment gross-profit contributions would help show whether the revenue mix is translating into profit. Finally, operating expenses, operating cash flow, property and equipment purchases, and free cash flow are useful indicators of expense control and cash conversion. These are monitoring points, not predictions.

memo.text:
Revenue was $28.05 billion, $7.48 billion below forecast. The largest shortfall came from automotive volume, which reduced revenue by $5.59 billion; services and other was $1.10 billion below forecast, and energy generation and storage was $720 million below forecast. These gaps outweighed the modest lift from automotive leasing, while regulatory credits were also slightly below forecast.
Gross profit was $5.49 billion, $1.14 billion below forecast. The gross-profit bridge shows automotive and energy as the main drags, partly offset by services; gross margin nevertheless finished 0.9 percentage points above forecast at 19.6%. Operating income was $718 million, $332.6 million below forecast, as the gross-profit shortfall exceeded the benefit from operating expenses coming in $807.8 million below forecast. Lower research and development and selling, general and administrative expenses contributed to that expense undershoot.
Free cash flow was $1.53 billion, $90.5 million above forecast. Operating cash flow exceeded forecast by $1.59 billion, more than offsetting property and equipment purchases that were $1.50 billion above forecast. The cash result therefore held up better than operating income, despite heavier capital spending.
